topic.name: Simplifying Square Root Expressions Using the Product Rule

question.explanation:
We first write $45y^2$ as the product $9y^2 \cdot 5$ which contains a perfect square $(9y^2).$ Then, we can separate the product into two separate radicals, one of which can be simplified: \[ \eqalign{ \sqrt{45y^2} &= \\[3pt] \sqrt{9y^2\cdot 5} &= \\[3pt] \sqrt{(3y)^2\cdot 5} &= \\[3pt] \sqrt{(3y)^2}\cdot \sqrt{5} &= \\[3pt] |3y|\cdot \sqrt{5}&= \\[3pt] |3|\cdot |y| \cdot \sqrt{5}&=\\[3pt] 3\cdot |y| \cdot \sqrt{5} } \]

Since $y \geq 0,$ we have $|y| = y,$ and we can simplify further. Therefore, our final answer is \[ \eqalign{ 3\cdot |y| \cdot \sqrt{5} &= \\[3pt] 3\cdot y \cdot \sqrt{5} &= \\[3pt] 3y\sqrt{5}. } \]

example.title: Simplifying a Radical Expression That Is Not a Perfect Square With Domain Restrictions

question.explanation: We first write $32a^7b^8$ as the product $16a^6b^8\cdot 2a$ which contains a perfect square $(16a^6b^8).$ Then, we separate the product into two separate radicals, one of which can be simplified: \[ \eqalign{ \sqrt{32a^7b^8}&=\\[3pt] \sqrt{16a^6b^8 \cdot 2a} &= \\[3pt] \sqrt{(4a^3b^4)^2\cdot 2a}&=\\[3pt] \sqrt{(4a^3b^4)^2}\cdot \sqrt{2a}&=\\[3pt] |4a^3b^4|\cdot\sqrt{2a}&=\\[3pt] |4|\cdot|a^3|\cdot|b^4|\cdot\sqrt{2a}&=\\[3pt] 4\cdot|a^3|\cdot|b^4|\cdot\sqrt{2a} } \] A number raised to the power of four is always positive or zero, and the absolute value of any positive (or zero) number is itself, so we have that $|b^4|=b^4$ and $|a^3| = a^3.$ Therefore, our final answer is \[ \eqalign{ 4\cdot|a^3|\cdot|b^4|\cdot\sqrt{2a}&=\\[3pt] 4\cdot a^3\cdot b^4\cdot\sqrt{2a}&=\\[3pt] 4a^3b^4\sqrt{2a}. } \]

example.title: Simplifying a Radical Expression That Is Not a Perfect Square With Domain Restrictions

question.explanation:
We first write $20n^5$ as the product $4n^4 \cdot 5n$ which contains a perfect square $(4n^4).$ Then, we can separate the product into two separate radicals, one of which can be simplified:

\[ \eqalign{ \sqrt{20n^5} &= \\[3pt] \sqrt{4n^4 \cdot 5n} &= \\[3pt] \sqrt{(2n^2)^2\cdot 5n}&=\\[3pt] \sqrt{(2n^2)^2} \cdot \sqrt{5n} &= \\[3pt] |2n^2| \cdot \sqrt{5n} &= \\[3pt] |2|\cdot |n^2|\cdot \sqrt{5n}&=\\[3pt] 2\cdot |n^2|\cdot \sqrt{5n} } \] A squared number is always positive or zero, and the absolute value of any positive (or zero) number is itself, so we have \begin{align*} 2\cdot |n^2|\cdot \sqrt{5n} &=\\[3pt] 2\cdot n^2\cdot\sqrt{5n}&=\\[3pt] 2n^2\sqrt{5n}. \end{align*}
